## Commit Message Instructions

Keep commit messages short and concise.

Start your commit message with a category from the list below to describe the purpose of the change.

Format: <category>: <message>

Examples:
  feat: add new search functionality
  fix: crash when uploading files

### Categories

data: Updates or adds data.
Example: data: update population dataset

fix: Fixes a user-facing bug.
Example: fix: broken link in footer

refactor: Changes code without fixing bugs or adding features.
Example: refactor: chart rendering logic

perf: Improves performance (speed, memory).
Example: perf: improve chart loading speed

feat: Adds a new user-facing feature.
Example: feat: add dark mode support

docs: Updates or adds documentation.
Example: docs: add setup guide for developers

chore: Maintenance tasks like dependency updates.
Example: chore: update Node.js to latest version

style: Formatting, commas, or whitespace changes (no logic change).
Example: style: fix inconsistent indentation

wip: Work In Progress.
Example: wip: initial layout for dashboard

test: Adds or refactors tests.
Example: test: add missing unit tests

---

### Tips
- Keep messages concise and clear.
- Use one emoji per commit for clarity.
- Split changes into separate commits if needed.
